review_note: Read the test and helper line by line. Hashes (receipt, manifest, test, all manifest files) match. The Mac console log shows 114 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, with all 6 'b31jb spatial' lines present. Totoro native run only skips (live test), so counts rest on the Mac log. Oracle: base-R dense Laplace with a hand-built exponential kernel (Euclidean distance, range equal to the median positive distance, 1e-6 jitter) from random irregular coordinates given in permuted row order. The package precision inverse is compared with the hand kernel at 1e-8. Agreement is 1.8e-6 to 3.9e-6 at the Julia estimates. Bug sensitivity: selector swap, SD sign, reversed SD, SD intercept shift, K x 2, max-distance range, and kernel by position all move the oracle. The smallest gap is 0.630 (logit intercept, max-distance range) against 1e-3, about x630. The optimum check passes. Rows: the three spatial_coordinate_intercept rows (logit, probit, cloglog) are supported. They fit spatial(1 | site, coords) with sd(site, level='spatial') ~ z, which is one structured field. The three spatial_coordinate_slope rows are NOT supported on the literal layout reading. The row layout is 'structured intercept plus one independent numeric slope' (independent coordinate fields), but the test fits only spatial(0 + x | site, coords), a slope-only field with no structured intercept field. The slope-only fit is oracle-correct. Earlier native slope-only tests were reviewed as covering this row label, so the orchestrator may overrule me by precedent. Does NOT establish: an intercept-plus-slope spatial layout (two independent fields), a correlated spatial block, mesh/SPDE kernels (this is the coordinate kernel only), calibration or coverage, other coordinate layouts, sizes or seeds, or native-engine behaviour. Lane rule (review-20261102.md, slope-only fits): the slope rows are linked as the slope member only; the verifier or reviewer objected that no structured intercept field is fitted in the same model, which is recorded here.
